title: Every `ia` consumer command refusal names one next command
summary: Every consumer command refusal now carries a next action: the --json refusal object always has a non-empty string next, where a refusal raised by a service used to carry null, and human output prints the same text on the → line without breaking the command it quotes across lines. The text quotes exactly one command and spells no other command or option beside it; remedies that used to list alternative flags or sources now name one command, and a service message may still name the alternatives. The command is an ia command, including transaction recovery through ia recover with an explicit --root. A directory registry repair still names ia-distribution, the binary of @inventarch/distribution, which a global install of @inventarch/cli does not put on PATH. It carries the values the invocation supplied that it needs, such as the root (the target directory for ia init), host, package ids, registry or catalog source, descriptor or --force. Except after an unknown or interrupted command, which repeat the invocation as typed (below), a command that reruns the refused one repeats no output flag such as --json, and a rerun of an install or update names its plan, without --apply; a rerun of ia restore carries --apply --yes, the rerun after deleting a corrupt cached archive drops --offline so the archive is fetched again, and a placeholder such as <directory>, <path>, <file> or <url|dir> stands only for the value to correct or supply. It may begin with one manual step, such as deleting a named file, replacing a link under .ia/src, mapping a provider in .ia/registries.json or setting IA_HOME. A workspace whose sources cannot be read, such as one with a link under .ia/src, names that repair and then ia validate for its root. A service refusal without a remedy of its own names the command's --help for a usage error, ia validate for a record finding (IA-COMP, IA-GRAPH and IA-LANG codes) and ia doctor for any other code, with the root the invocation gave. An unknown command names the nearest one with the rest of the invocation as typed, keeping only --root and --params for a machine operation. A file the invocation named that is not there (the --descriptor of ia pack, the --catalog or --requests of ia install, update and restore) names the same command with that one value as <file>. ia host with a --root that does not exist now refuses as IA-DB-ROOT-INVALID, as every other command does, instead of IA-CLI-FAILED: it used to fail inside its own error handling, so the exit class stays 3 and only the defect's code changes. An interrupted command (exit 130) gains next in its JSON object and on its stderr line: the rerun that finishes work the command had already written, or otherwise the same invocation as typed, with any --apply, --yes and --json it was given. Many next texts are reworded, so automation should match the code, not the sentence. ia compile, deprecated in favour of ia capture and otherwise unchanged in 1.x (its alias of ia capture lands in 2.0), keeps every refusal's code, exit class and location: an existing artifact without --force names the same invocation with --force, an --out outside .ia/work/ names it with --out <file>, and --out with --stdout names ia compile --help. The nine machine protocol operations and their output are unchanged. Code that imports the published internal subpaths keeps its 1.x forms: in @inventarch/cli/internal/consumer the Refusal constructor's where and next still default to null, refusalOf(error) without the refused invocation still returns a null next, and renderRefusal gains an optional refused argument and gives a refusal without a next action the fallback above, so the --json next is a string even then; refusalOf(error, refused) spells that fallback itself. In @inventarch/cli/internal/distribute, PlanRequest gains an optional reruns field; without it collectPlan spells each remedy's command from the request's own fields, and every refusal keeps its code. The exported UNMAPPED text is unchanged. In the 1.x collectPlan request form, a missing --catalog or --requests file now throws the CLI Refusal, with the same code IA-DIST-INPUT-INVALID and exit 3 and a next, where it threw the service DistributionError; collectPlan already threw Refusal for its other refusals in 1.x, so callers should match the code.
